source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Update BIOS/BMC to the approved latest firmware, physically swap CPUs, power on, prove BIOS and OS boot, and confirm correct CPU information in both environments.
procedure_facts: Flash BIOS and BMC to `laste FW`.
criteria_facts: If the system repeatedly reboots during POST after the swap, inspect the BMC power policy and change it to Off; the source marks this as an issue.
BIOS and OS must detect correct CPU information.
source_conflicts: `Swap CPUs` does not define whether two installed processors exchange sockets, a processor is replaced with another part, or a processor is removed and reinstalled.
`Latest FW` is not a reproducible BIOS/BMC version and the source does not state whether firmware flashing is conditional or separately qualified.

The criterion mentions changing BMC power policy to Off during repeated POST reboot but does not define the exact property, intended steady-state value, approval or restoration; it is an issue response, not an automatic pass step.
missing_source_information: Pre-to-post CPU/socket swap matrix with physical part/serial/asset identifiers or another unique traceability method.
Supported CPU/stepping/microcode/population matrix and board-specific socket, heatsink, torque and thermal-material procedure.
Exact approved BIOS/BMC versions, images, checksums, flashing order and recovery.
Expected BIOS/SMBIOS/OS CPU model, socket, core/thread, NUMA and status values after the swap.
BMC power-policy object/value, reason for Off, persistence/restoration rule and repeated-POST stop threshold.

original_test_intent.statement: Validate that the server remains bootable and correctly enumerates its CPU population in BIOS and OS after the specifically approved physical CPU swap, with the platform on the required BIOS/BMC firmware and with repeated-POST behavior handled as a controlled issue.
must_preserve: The exact engineer-defined physical CPU swap, not a software-only inventory check.
Required BIOS/BMC firmware state before the swap.
Power-on and successful BIOS then OS boot.
Correct per-socket CPU information in BIOS and OS.
Detection and controlled handling of repeated POST reboot.
One swap operation and 30/30-minute planning estimates.
must_not_infer: The direction or meaning of the swap without a matrix.
That `latest` means any newest public image or authorizes an upgrade.
That two identical-model CPUs can be individually traced using model/core fields alone.
That a BMC power-policy change is automatically safe or part of PASS.
That OS inventory alone proves BIOS detection, mechanical installation or thermal integrity.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly classifies the essential CPU exchange as MANUAL ONLY, retains automated post-swap inventory as supporting evidence, requires qualified physical/firmware recovery and forbids automatic BMC policy changes.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 never resolves what is being swapped and its filtered `lscpu`/`dmidecode` output cannot prove individual pre/post socket movement or full CPU correctness. It needs an explicit swap matrix and unfiltered per-socket evidence; SMBIOS itself must not be treated as unquestionable physical truth.

related_records: No other CPU inventory or swap case can define this row's physical part mapping, supported population or firmware target.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Preserve V2's MANUAL ONLY boundary because the physical exchange is the core action. Treat firmware, CPU compatibility and BMC policy as owner-supplied platform facts and do not turn post-swap software collection into proof that the manual swap occurred as intended.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep MANUAL ONLY because a qualified operator must perform the CPU work and any approved firmware update. V3 adds the missing pre/post socket-part swap matrix, separates physical proof from BIOS/SMBIOS/OS reports, and treats repeated POST reboot/power-policy change as a stop-and-escalate condition rather than an automatic workaround.

conditions_present: Physical CPU swap, firmware prerequisite, power-on, BIOS/OS boot and CPU-information acceptance are stated.
missing: Swap meaning/matrix, unique CPU traceability, compatibility/population and service procedure, exact firmware artifacts, expected topology, POST threshold, power-policy semantics, approvals and recovery.
provider: Platform/CPU owner supplies the swap matrix, CPU support/population and socket/heatsink/thermal service procedure.
BIOS/BMC owners supply approved versioned images/checksums, update need/order and recovery.
Lab/test owner supplies outage approval, operator, evidence rules, expected topology and issue disposition.
safe_read_only_work: Collect pre-swap CPU socket/topology/NUMA, SMBIOS type 4, firmware, BMC power policy, SEL, boot and thermal baselines.
Verify CPU part/stepping support, signed swap map, firmware artifacts/checksums and recovery offline.
After the operator completes the swap and boot, collect BIOS-console evidence plus full `lscpu` and `dmidecode -t 4` outputs without changing state.
prohibited_until_resolved: Firmware flashing, chassis opening, CPU/heatsink removal, socket handling, power cycling, automatic power-policy modification, repeated reboot attempts or PASS.
closure_evidence: A signed matrix uniquely identifies the pre/post CPU-to-socket mapping and whether the operation is exchange, replacement or reseat.
Approved firmware target/images, compatibility, mechanical/thermal procedure and recovery are ready.
Expected BIOS/OS per-socket topology and controlled repeated-POST issue procedure are documented.

revision_candidate.test_name: Validate BIOS and OS CPU Enumeration After the Approved Physical CPU Swap
revision_candidate.purpose: Confirm that, after one engineer-defined physical CPU exchange/replacement/reseat and any separately approved BIOS/BMC update, the server completes POST, enters BIOS, boots the OS and reports the expected CPU population and topology for every socket without new CPU, socket, thermal or firmware errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the board revision, CPU models/steppings, socket population, heatsink/thermal assembly, BIOS/BMC images and OS/kernel in the signed recipe. The physical operation follows the exact vendor service procedure; post-swap commands run on the host OS and BIOS evidence comes from console/setup, not from OS inference.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The sockets and physical CPUs listed in the signed pre/post swap matrix, one swap operation and the ensuing BIOS/OS boot/identification result. It does not add CPU stress, performance or long-duration thermal qualification. Any firmware flash is only the source-required prerequisite and must use exact approved artifacts. Treat 30/30 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: SUT/board identity; explicit swap type; pre/post socket-to-CPU matrix and a mandatory owner-approved traceability method. Use a readable processor serial/part/asset identifier when available; otherwise use socket-labelled before/after package-marking photos plus witnessed chain-of-custody or owner-controlled temporary asset labels. For an exchange, prove both CPUs moved to the specified opposite sockets; for a replacement, identify removed and installed parts; for a reseat, prove the same CPU returned to the same socket. Also require supported CPU/stepping/microcode/population rules; vendor ESD/socket/heatsink/torque/thermal-material procedure; qualified operator; shutdown/de-energize and power-on plan; exact BIOS/BMC versions, signed images/checksums, flash need/order and recovery; expected per-socket BIOS/SMBIOS/OS topology; console/OOB access; BMC power-policy object/value and issue procedure; boot timeout/attempt limit; evidence storage and approval.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Before disruption, capture the full CPU/socket/NUMA, SMBIOS type-4, firmware, power-policy, SEL, thermal and boot baseline and reconcile it to the signed swap matrix. Flash only exact approved firmware if the recipe requires a change, then verify versions and health. A qualified operator powers down/de-energizes the SUT and performs the one documented CPU operation with physical part/socket evidence. After power-on, capture POST and BIOS CPU information before booting the OS. In the OS, collect unfiltered `lscpu`, a parseable per-CPU/socket/core/node mapping and complete `dmidecode -t 4`; compare each source with the expected matrix and record any SMBIOS limitation. Stop on repeated POST reboot; inspect but do not change BMC policy unless a separately approved issue procedure directs it.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Non-production SUT; correct target and swap matrix; CPUs/board/firmware compatible; firmware images and rollback validated; approved outage; workloads stopped; qualified operator, ESD and board-specific mechanical/thermal tools available; platform fully de-energized per service procedure; console/OOB and recovery ready; baseline healthy; expected topology and POST thresholds signed.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: SUT/board identity; signed operation type and pre/post CPU-to-socket matrix; the selected traceability record: readable processor/owner asset identifiers, or socket-labelled package-marking photos plus witnessed chain-of-custody/temporary labels. Evidence must prove both directions for an exchange, removed-versus-installed identity for a replacement, or same-part/same-socket custody for a reseat. Also collect compatibility and service-procedure revision; operator ESD/mechanical/thermal checklist; exact firmware image hashes/update transcript and verified versions if flashed; power-down/up record; POST and BIOS per-socket CPU evidence; complete pre/post `lscpu`, parseable CPU/socket/core/NUMA map and full SMBIOS type-4 output; expected/actual comparison; CPU status/microcode/thermal health; SEL/dmesg/journal boot errors; BMC policy value and any issue handling; engineer disposition.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The signed operation-specific swap matrix, approved traceability method, platform CPU/firmware support recipe, board service procedure and expected BIOS/OS topology. Pass requires the intended exchange, replacement or reseat to be proven by the selected physical/custody record, BIOS and OS to boot, every populated socket to report the expected CPU/status/topology and no disallowed CPU/socket/thermal/firmware errors; model-name output or undocumented operator recollection alone is insufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not automate or remotely simulate the physical swap, open energized hardware, improvise CPU/heatsink/thermal work, flash an unversioned `latest` image, infer unique CPU movement from identical model strings, truncate inventory before comparison, keep cycling through POST failures or silently change BMC power policy. Stop on wrong part/socket, bent/damaged socket, torque/thermal deviation, firmware mismatch/update failure, abnormal power/thermal indication, repeated POST reboot, missing CPU, topology mismatch or boot failure.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform owner approves the exact swap and compatibility; BIOS/BMC owners approve any flash and recovery; lab owner authorizes outage and physical work; qualified operator performs and records the hardware procedure; engineer authorizes any BMC policy change/reseat/reflash and judges PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: CPU identification, shutdown, chassis access, heatsink/CPU removal/installation, thermal assembly, visual/socket checks, power-on and BIOS observation are human/qualified-operator work. An Agent may validate artifacts and collect/compare pre/post firmware, SMBIOS, OS topology and logs after each human handoff; it cannot replace physical proof.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On firmware failure, use only the signed BIOS/BMC recovery path. On socket/CPU/thermal or POST failure, stop power cycles, preserve console/SEL evidence, de-energize and let the qualified owner inspect/reseat/restore the approved configuration. Do not change BMC power policy or flash another image without a new authorized recovery step; revalidate firmware, mapping, thermals, BIOS and OS after recovery.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Swap type/matrix or an operation-appropriate traceability method is missing; processor identifiers are unavailable and no socket-labelled photo plus witnessed/owner-controlled custody method has been approved; compatibility, service procedure, firmware targets/images, expected topology, qualified operator, outage approval or recovery is missing; hardware cannot be safely de-energized; physical damage/installation deviation occurs; firmware verification fails; POST repeats beyond the signed limit; BMC policy differs unexpectedly; BIOS or OS misses/misidentifies a CPU; topology/NUMA/core/thread/status mismatches; thermal/SEL/OS errors appear; or required physical/BIOS/OS evidence is absent.

identified_defects: The source does not define the meaning or direction of `Swap CPUs`.
V2's filtered inventory is insufficient for per-socket topology and unique CPU traceability.
`Latest FW` is not a reproducible or automatically authorized target.
SMBIOS reports BIOS-provided data and may not uniquely identify identical processors; it cannot replace operator physical records.
The BMC power-policy instruction is ambiguous and unsafe as an automatic workaround.
reason_for_change: Retain the essential manual boundary while making the CPU movement, firmware prerequisite and evidence independently traceable instead of treating filtered model/socket strings as proof of an undefined swap.

new_technical_evidence.title: lscpu(1)
new_technical_evidence.supports: lscpu derives architecture/topology from sysfs, `/proc/cpuinfo` and architecture libraries and can report sockets, cores, threads, NUMA, model, stepping and microcode; parseable explicit columns are preferable because default output may change.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Supported columns and the platform's expected topology must be supplied.

new_technical_evidence.title: dmidecode
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BIOS-reported SMBIOS processor information after the swap
new_technical_evidence.supports: dmidecode reports what BIOS exposes, including socket status and possibly serial/part data, but the project warns DMI data can be unreliable and must not be blindly trusted; it therefore complements rather than replaces physical and BIOS-console evidence.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Whether this platform populates unique processor serial/part fields is unknown.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00113-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The firmware prerequisite, physical swap, power-on, BIOS/OS boot, CPU-information check and repeated-POST/BMC-policy issue note.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Swap mapping, firmware versions, expected topology and policy procedure are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Requires the engineer to choose exchange, replacement or reseat and record a pre/post socket map.
Separates operator proof of physical CPU movement from BIOS/SMBIOS/OS enumeration.
Replaces `latest` with exact approved firmware artifacts.
Makes repeated POST reboot a stop/escalation condition rather than an automatic policy edit.
resolved_blockers: The manual CPU work is executable by a qualified operator and automated evidence collection remains useful; the case is MANUAL ONLY, not semantically BLOCKED.
remaining_blockers: Execution requires the exact swap matrix, compatibility/service procedure, firmware artifacts, expected topology, issue-policy rule, qualified operator, approval and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 proves the requested physical change with a source-specific socket/part matrix and full BIOS/OS topology evidence, avoiding V2's false implication that filtered model strings can identify an undefined CPU swap or that SMBIOS alone is physical truth.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The first contract-only validation found a document contradiction: unique traceability was mandatory, but physical identifiers were requested only when available. V3 was revised to require an operation-specific physical or custody method for exchange, replacement or reseat, including socket-labelled photos plus witnessed/owner-controlled custody when unique serials are absent. Revalidation found the contradiction resolved with no remaining document defect.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 156 requires firmware state, a physical CPU swap, power-on, BIOS/OS boot and correct CPU information, with repeated POST reboot tied to a BMC policy issue.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 preserves the manual boundary but never defines the swap map and uses filtered software inventory that cannot prove movement of identical CPUs between sockets.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow artifact and baseline collection before disruption; require qualified manual work and exact firmware/swap/topology handoff, then use full BIOS/SMBIOS/OS evidence without automatically changing power policy.
